stories.head: From Found to Cited: How AI Agents Are Replacing Human Web Visitors
stories.plain: The article argues that AI agents acting on behalf of consumers are now the most important 'visitors' to your site — meaning brands must optimize for being cited inside AI-generated answers, not just ranked in traditional search. This reframes SEO strategy entirely and has direct budget and content-production implications for marketing teams.

stories.head: 27 Holiday Shopping Statistics for 2026: AI Agents and Cyber Week Trends
stories.plain: A sourced data roundup showing how AI shopping agents are reshaping consumer behavior during peak retail seasons. Marketers planning holiday campaigns need to understand how autonomous agents are intercepting purchase decisions before a human ever reaches a brand's site or ad — changing where and how to compete for attention.

stories.head: ZoomInfo acquires DoubleO.ai and launches Agent Teams for autonomous GTM execution
stories.plain: ZoomInfo bought AI-agent startup DoubleO.ai and shipped Agent Teams, a product that coordinates multiple AI agents across a company's data and systems to run full go-to-market plays — from spotting a signal to taking action — with no human babysitting each step. This changes how revenue teams buy and deploy sales-marketing automation at scale.

stories.head: Braze expands AI from content creation to campaign operations and external LLM connections
stories.plain: Braze added AI decisioning tools that automate campaign health checks and let marketers pipe in external LLMs like Anthropic's Claude. This matters because it moves a major CEP beyond copy generation into operational AI — shifting how marketers buy and configure engagement platforms.

stories.head: Jellyfish research shows AI shopping assistants create entirely different competitive 'shelves', launches Share of Model optimization
stories.plain: Jellyfish found that AI shopping assistants surface radically different product sets than traditional search, reshuffling brand leadership and price positioning. They're launching a 'Share of Model' measurement product to help marketers understand and influence what AI recommends — a direct challenge to conventional search and retail media strategies.

stories.head: DataDome joins Experian Agent Trust ecosystem to verify AI agent intent continuously during agentic commerce
stories.plain: Experian's Agent Trust platform now uses DataDome to check not just who an AI agent claims to represent, but whether its actions stay consistent with what it was authorized to do throughout a transaction. This is foundational governance infrastructure for any brand letting AI agents transact on customers' behalf.

stories.head: Salesforce acquires AI customer research startup Listen Labs
stories.plain: Salesforce bought Listen Labs, whose platform runs AI-simulated customer interviews and behavioral analysis. Folding this into Salesforce's CRM and agent stack means marketers could get real-time synthetic customer insight baked into the same platform running their campaigns — changing what 'knowing your customer' costs and requires.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: From Found to Cited by AI: Search Visibility Rewrites Its Rules
body: AI-powered search engines no longer surface ten blue links — they synthesise an answer and cite a handful of sources. That means ranking in a traditional sense is less valuable than being the source a generative model trusts enough to quote, a fundamentally different optimisation target that requires structured authority signals, visual assets, and schema rather than keyword density.

Myth-busting data confirms that many assumptions carried over from classic SEO simply do not hold in generative engines. Brands that continue optimising for click-through will find themselves invisible in AI answers, while those who reframe content as citable evidence — precise, attributed, and multimodal — capture the new zero-click citation slot.
ev: Agile Brand · From Found to Cited
MarTech · Visual SEO for AI search

themes.head: AI Agents Run Amok: Governance Becomes the Urgent Priority
body: Go-to-market teams are deploying AI agents faster than they can inventory them, creating a sprawl of autonomous actions that nobody fully tracks. ZoomInfo's acquisition of DoubleO.ai to launch Agent Teams and DataDome's integration with Experian's Agent Trust ecosystem both signal that the market is now scrambling to build the oversight layer that should have come first.

IBM's self-hosted deployment for AI sovereignty and Experian's continuous intent verification show that governance, provenance, and trust verification are emerging as genuine product categories — not compliance afterthoughts. Marketers who treat agent orchestration as a pure efficiency play without audit trails will accumulate invisible risk in their pipelines.
ev: MarTech · GTM teams losing track of AI agents

themes.head: AI Raises the Bar While Squeezing Tolerance for Failure
body: Consumers now experience AI-native convenience everywhere — instant answers, hyper-relevant recommendations, frictionless checkout — and they carry those expectations into every brand interaction. The result is a compressed tolerance window: a single clunky experience that would have been forgiven two years ago now triggers churn because the mental benchmark has shifted upward.

Mixbook's deliberate choice to hide the word 'AI' from customer messaging while still leveraging it deeply is a leading signal: the brands winning this moment are those using AI to deliver emotional resonance and permanence, not those waving it as a feature flag. Speed of production must be matched by quality of outcome or the gap becomes a brand liability.
ev: MarTech · AI makes customers expect more
Agile Brand · Mixbook CEO on permanence & AI
MarTech · AI made marketing faster not better

themes.head: B2B's Evidence Gap: Proving Pipeline in an AI-Shaped Buyer Journey
body: B2B marketing's credibility crisis is not a measurement technology problem — it is a failure to build and present the right evidence to CFOs and boards. As AI reshapes the buyer journey by collapsing research stages and shifting brand discovery into AI chat interfaces, the traditional funnel attribution models produce data that no longer maps to how deals actually form.

Circle & Square's buyer intelligence guide and Growth7's CRM-to-pipeline platform both point to the same response: richer first-party intent signals, tied to revenue outcomes, not activity metrics. CMOs who can reconstruct a coherent evidence chain through the new AI-mediated journey will own the boardroom conversation; those who cannot will keep losing budget.
ev: Agile Brand · CMOs & AI-shaped B2B journey

themes.head: Retail Media Grows Up: From Banner to Full-Funnel Experience
body: Retail media is moving beyond sponsored product listings into experiential, in-aisle, and full-funnel formats that blend the physical and digital. CommerceIQ's AI-powered expansion to Chewy Ads and Particular Audience's trade media solution show that the category is now sophisticated enough to manage inventory, creative, and measurement in a single automated layer.

Comcast's research confirming that TV and streaming drive results across the entire buyer journey reinforces that channel convergence — not channel siloing — is the strategic imperative. Brands that unify retail media, CTV, and in-store signals into one attribution view will capture both the impulse moment and the long-term brand equity that sustains price positioning.
ev: MarTech Series · Comcast TV & streaming buyer journey

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack this month, the central pressure is the same: AI is simultaneously raising customer expectations, collapsing old measurement frameworks, and demanding new governance disciplines — and the brands that will pull ahead are those treating all three as one integrated strategic problem rather than three separate vendor decisions.
